questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which statement is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: The term “homeostasis” describes maintenance of nearly constant conditions in the internal environment

options.label: B
options.text: In most disease conditions, homeostatic mechanisms are no longer operating in the body

options.label: C
options.text: The body’s compensatory mechanisms often lead to deviations from the normal range in some of the body functions

options.label: D
options.text: Disease is generally considered to be a state of disrupted homeostasis

questions.answerText: In most disease conditions, homeostatic mechanisms are no longer operating in the body
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

In most disease conditions, homeostatic mechanisms are no longer operating in the body.

Homeostasis is the maintenance of nearly constant conditions in the internal environment. Disease is generally considered to be a state of disrupted homeostasis. However, even in diseased states the body’s homeostatic compensatory mechanisms are functional and continue to operate to sustain body functions at levels that permit life to continue. These compensatory mechanisms can result in deviations from the normal range in some of the body functions.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for producing adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the energy currency of the cell?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Mitochondria

Mitochondria are called the “powerhouses” of the cell and contain oxidative enzymes that permit oxidation of the nutrients liberating energy that is used to synthesize “high-energy” ATP.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: 60% of the total body water in is which of the following compartments?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Intracellular

Two-thirds of the total body water is in the ICF.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following are best suited to measure the intracellular fluid volume?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Heavy water and inulin

Measurement of ICF is indirect. ICF = TBW – ECF. Heavy water is most used for measurement of total body eater and Inulin is the most accurate for measurement of ECF volume. A combination of heavy water and inulin is best suited for measurement of ICF.

Radioactive sodium is used for ECF measurement.

Radioactive iodine labelled albumin is used for measurement of plasma volume.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 70-year old man has congestive cardiac failure. His cardiac output is 4L/min, bp is 110/80 mm Hg and heart rate is 90/minute. Further tests reveal that his right atrial pressure is 10 mm Hg. Which of the following will be expected to increase in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Increase in RAP to 10 mm Hg decreases the venous return to the heart and therefore, increase the vena cava hydrostatic pressure. This in turn increases the tissue capillary hydrostatic pressure, especially in the capillaries of the lower limb (if patient is ambulant), leading to pedal edema.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The equation which is used to calculate the magnitude of the equilibrium potential of a freely diffusible ion is which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Donnan and Gibbs showed that in the presence of a non-diffusible ion, the diffusible ions distribute themselves so that at equilibrium their concentration ratios are equal. This is the Gibbs Donnan Equation.

If a membrane is freely permeable to an ion, magnitude of potential difference for that ion at equilibrium (equilibrium potential or Nernst potential) can be calculated by the Nernst Equation.

Goldmann Hodgkin Katz equation is used to calculate the RMP.

Henderson Hasselbach equation is used to calculate the pH of a buffer solution containing given concentrations of an acid and its conjugate base.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Gibbs- Donnan equilibrium is based on which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Intracellular proteins

Donnan and Gibbs showed that in the presence of a non-diffusible ion (proteins), a pair of diffusible ions distribute themselves so that at equilibrium, their concentration ratios are equal:

This is the Gibbs- Donnan equation. It is applicable for any pair of cations and anions of the same valence.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: If alveolar surface area is decreased by 50% and pulmonary fibrosis leads to doubling of diffusion distance, how will the diffusion of O2 be affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

decreases by 75%

Diffusion of gases across the respiratory membrane follows the Fick’s law of diffusion.

Net transport

= - (diffusion coefficient) (surface area) (concentration gradient)/ (thickness of membrane)

Transport is directly proportional to surface area and inverse to the thickness of membrane. If the surface area is decreased to half and thickness of membrane is doubled, transport is decreases to one-fourth or in other words, decreases by 75%.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following has similar values for both ICF and ISF?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

total osmolality

Colloid osmotic pressure is determine by proteins, which are much higher in the ICF than ISF. Colloid osmotic pressure is higher in ICF.

Potassium is higher in ICF.

Sodium is higher in ISF.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Hypertonic 3% saline contains how much of Na+ in meq/l?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

513

1 equivalent of a substance = 1 mole of that substance/ (No. of metal ions) X (valence)

For NaCl, 1 equivalent = 1 mole

3% NaCl = 3 gm of NaCl in 100mL = 30 gm of NaCl in 1000mL

58.5 gm of NaCl = 1 mole of NaCl

30 gm of NaCl = 30/58.5 mole = 0.513 mole = 513 millimole = 513 milliequivalent

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion share which of the following characteristics?

options.label: D
options.text: Can be blocked by specific transporters

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion are examples of passive transport and therefore, do not require energy for transport.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Most important buffer in the interstitial fluid is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

Bicarbonate

The principal buffer in the interstitial fluid is bicarbonate.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Excess blood is transfused into a patient whose mean arterial pressure increases from 100 to 125 mm Hg. After correction, the patient’s blood pressure is 105 mm Hg. What is the “gain”?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

-4

Gain = Correction / error

Since the MAP lowers from 125 to 105 mm Hg, the correction is -20mm Hg. Here the minus sign does not have a mathematical significance. It simple means that the corrected blood pressure is lower.

The error is +5 mm Hg. The plus sign here indicates that the corrected blood pressure is higher than the normal MAP.

Gain = -20/+4 = -4

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which statement about feedback control systems is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Most control systems in the body act by negative feedback

options.label: C
options.text: Generation of nerve action potentials involves positive feedback

options.label: D
options.text: Feed- forward is important in regulating motor activity

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Positive feedback systems are stabilizing.

Most control systems in the body act by negative feedback mechanisms and these are stabilizing. They help maintain homeostasis.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following are involved in tight junctions except
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

connexins

Connexins form “gap junctions”.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following are true about gap junctions except

options.label: A
options.text: Gap junctions form a cytoplasmic “tunnel” for diffusion of small molecules (1000 Da) between two neighbouring cells

options.label: B
options.text: Gap junctions are formed by proteins called connexons

options.label: C
options.text: Connexons in the membrane of one cell are lined up with connexons of a neighbouring cell to form dodecameric gap junctions

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

Gap junctions form chemical synapses

Gap junctions form electrical synapses. They for a low resistance path for bi-directional movement of ions, molecules, sugars and amino acids less than 1000 Daltons.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following are present on the alpha subunit of the sodium potassium ATPase pump except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

glycosylation site

Glycosylation site is on the beta subunit.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is true about endocytosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Includes phagocytosis and pinocytosis, but not clathrin- mediated or caveolae dependent uptake of extracellular contents

options.label: B
options.text: Refers to merging of an intracellular vesicle with the plasma membrane to deliver vesicular contents to the ECF

options.label: C
options.text: Refers to the invagination of the cell membrane to uptake extracellular contents into the cell

options.label: D
options.text: Refers vesicular trafficking between Golgi apparatus

questions.answerText: Refers to the invagination of the cell membrane to uptake extracellular contents into the cell
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

Refers to the invagination of the cell membrane to uptake extracellular contents into the cell. It includes phagocytosis (“cell eating”) and pinocytosis (“cell drinking”), clathrin- mediated endocytosis and caveolae dependent uptake of extracellular contents.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following mechanisms for transport across the luminal cell membrane of an enterocyte is present in newborns and infants but not in adults?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Intestinal absorption of immunoglobulins (in colostrum) during early infancy occurs by endocytosis. This ability to absorb large molecules by endocytosis occurs during the first several months of life but is lost thereafter. Simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion, primary and secondary active transports are all normal processes in enterocytes.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is higher in the ICF?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

K+

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following describes infinite feedback gain principle?

options.label: A
options.text: Negative feedback system with error of zero

options.label: B
options.text: Negative feedback system with correction of zero

options.label: C
options.text: Negative feedback system with gain of zero

options.label: D
options.text: There is no such thing as infinite gain in a feedback system

questions.answerText: Negative feedback system with error of zero
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Negative feedback system with error of zero

For a negative feedback system,

Gain = correction/ error

If error is zero, the gain is infinite.

The control of arterial pressure by the renal- body fluid mechanism, where the arterial pressure always exactly comes back to equilibrium point, makes it an example of infinite feedback gain principle.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following cell organelle does not have a limiting membrane?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

nucleolus

The nucleolus does not have a limiting membrane. Nuclei of most cells contain one or more highly staining structures called nucleoli. Nucleolus is simple an accumulation of large amounts of RNA and proteins. The nucleolus becomes considerably enlarged when the cell is actively synthesizing proteins.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The most important factor which determines the movement of a permeant substance across the cell membrane is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Diffusion coefficient of a substance is determined mainly by the lipid solubility of that substance.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: In an ideal solution, which of the following is correct? (P is osmotic pressure, n is number of particles, R is gas constant, T is absolute temperature, V is volume)
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

P = nRT/V. If T is constant, osmotic pressure is proportional to the number of particles in solution per unit volume of the solution.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: The following graph shows the transport kinetics of a solute transferred across cell membrane What is the likely nature of the solute :
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

Since carrier proteins tend to get saturated all carrier mediated transports will have a transport maxima. Glucose is transported by facilitated diffusion which is carrier mediated. Therefore, transport of glucose will show a transport maxima.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The blood-cytoplasm gradient generated by pump or leak systems is maximum for which of the following
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

The blood: cytoplasm ratio for Na+ is 12:1, for K+ it is 1:35, for H+ it is 1:2.5, for Ca++ it is 18,000:1.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: In a clinical study to study the actions of an unknown test solution on RBC volume, 1 mL of heparinized blood is added into 100mL of test solution and mixed. Results show that the RBCs placed into the test solution immediately sell and burst. Into which of the following test solutions were the RBCs placed (intracellular osmolality is 280mosmol/L)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

140mmol of glucose

If the RBCs swell and burst then they must have been added to a hypotonic solution. 140mmol of glucose is equal to 140mosmol of glucose, which is hypotonic.

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Using the following data, calculate the filtration coefficient for the capillary bed. Plasma colloid osmotic pressure = 30 mm Hg Capillary hydrostatic pressure = 40 mm Hg Interstitial colloid osmotic pressure = 5 mm Hg Interstitial hydrostatic pressure = 5 mm Hg Rate of tissue fluid formation = 150mL/min
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

15mL/ min/ mm Hg

Rate of tissue fluid formation = Filtration coefficient X (Pc – πc – Pi + πi)

150mL/ min = Filtration coefficient X (40 – 30 – 5 + 5)mm Hg

Filtration coefficient = 150/10 = 15mL/ min/ mm Hg

questions.topic: DAMS · General Physiology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: Match the following cell organelle with its function
questions.solutionHtml:
A-4; B-5; C- 1; D-3

Agranular or smooth endoplasmic reticulum is involved in synthesis of lipids.

Granular or rough ER has ribosomes attached to its outer surface. The ribosomes are composed of a mixture of RNA and proteins, and they function to synthesize new protein molecules in the cell.

Golgi apparatus- Secreted proteins are condensed, sorted and packaged into secretory vesicles in the terminal portion of the Golgi apparatus, also k/a trans-Golgi network. It is here that proteins destined for secretion are separated from those destined for intracellular compartments or cellular membranes.

Lysosomes- Autophagy is a housekeeping process by which obsolete organelles and large protein aggregates are degraded and recycled by lysosomes. Lysosomes contain hydrolases that provide an intracellular digestive system that allows the cell to digest damaged cellular structures, food particles ingested by the cell and unwanted matter, such as bacteria.

All gene transcription occurs in the nucleus, regardless of the final destination of the protein product. The resulting m-RNA is transported through the nuclear pores in the nuclear membrane and translated into either the cytosol or the lumen of the RER.

Mitochondria are k/a powerhouse of a cell and are involved in generation of ATP.

Peroxisomes are involved in catabolism of long-chain fatty acids. Peroxisomes contain oxidases that help form H2O2, an oxidising agent, that helps to oxidise many substances that may be harmful to the cell (such as, alcohol).
